verdict: Williams grew revenue 10% to $3.2B as new power and pipeline projects and the Momentum acquisition lifted its fee-based business, with Adjusted EBITDA up 6% to $2.0B.

segments.name: Transmission, Power & Gulf
segments.note: External revenue from the Transco and Northwest Pipeline systems, Gulf gathering, power generation and storage — lifted by new power revenues, projects placed in service and higher storage rates.

segments.name: Northeast G&P
segments.note: External gathering and processing revenue in the Marcellus and Utica shale regions of the Northeast.

segments.name: West
segments.note: External gathering, processing and NGL revenue in the West — boosted by the Momentum Midstream acquisition (closed September 3, 2026) and the Louisiana Energy Gateway.

segments.name: Gas & NGL Marketing Services
segments.note: External revenue from marketing natural gas and NGLs, including a $29M net gain on commodity derivatives.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Upstream, corporate and other external revenues — down after the January 2026 sale of the South Mansfield upstream interests.

opex.name: Operating and maintenance
opex.note: Running pipelines, compressor stations and processing plants day to day, including property and other non-income taxes.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of pipelines, plants and equipment over their working lives.

opex.name: General, administrative & other, net
opex.note: General and administrative costs of $275M plus $4M of other operating expense, less an $83M gain on the sale of a Permian gathering system.

otherDetail: Equity earnings of $157M from pipeline and midstream joint ventures, plus $30M of other investing income and $50M of other income, less $385M of interest expense — a net $148M drag below operating income.
oneTimers: Operating income includes an $83M gain on the sale of a Permian gathering system; excluding this and other adjustments, adjusted net income was $663M, or $0.54 per share (non-GAAP), versus GAAP EPS of $0.56.
Williams closed the acquisition of Momentum Midstream (M6 Midstream) on September 3, 2026, strengthening its position in the Haynesville shale basin.

takeaways.title: Growth projects are paying off
takeaways.text: Service revenues rose $198M year on year on new power generation revenues, the Momentum acquisition, projects placed in service and higher storage revenues.

takeaways.title: On track for the top half of guidance
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $2.04B in Q3 and 9% year to date to $6.2B, and Williams says it is tracking toward the upper half of its $8.3B–$8.5B full-year 2026 range.

takeaways.title: Dividend well covered
takeaways.text: Available funds from operations rose 10% to $1.59B, covering the dividend 2.42 times, while Williams placed four pipeline expansions into service and upsized Transco projects in the quarter.

footerNote: Chart layout adapts Williams' printed statement: product costs ($618M) plus net processing commodity expenses ($14M) form the direct-cost block. Segment figures are external revenues by reportable segment from the Form 10-Q (sales between segments excluded, so they sum to consolidated revenue); Williams' reported segment totals including internal sales were $3,523M. Net income is the consolidated $767M; $700M was attributable to Williams common stockholders after $67M attributable to noncontrolling interests and $1M of preferred dividends.
